answer: Distinct-channel binding.** Each identity must own a unique physical sensor channel—say a camera whose lens carries a factory-etched pigment pattern—registered by hash. The registry builds a trellis of verified channel lineages, and every agent action must bridge to a live channel reading within a freshness window. Creating a second identity requires acquiring another distinct physical device, so an attacker's cost is hardware plus enrollment latency per identity, not just a deposit.
